subject.title: fix(cli): bound dns setup subprocess calls with timeout

question: Should `openclaw dns setup` use a single 30-second hard kill for Homebrew and sudo commands, or should it use command-aware handling that preserves legitimate package-manager setup time?
rationale: The code change deliberately trades an unbounded wait for a strict setup deadline; repository evidence does not establish that 30 seconds is safe for all supported Homebrew paths.

options.title: Use command-aware bounds
options.body: Keep a short bound only for commands proven to be quick and use a demonstrably safe bounded strategy for package-manager work.

options.title: Accept the 30-second deadline
options.body: Land the uniform deadline and explicitly accept that slow Homebrew setup may require rerunning the command.

options.title: Pause for DNS setup evidence
options.body: Hold this PR until a maintainer can validate expected Homebrew and sudo timing on supported setup paths.

recommendation.title: Use command-aware bounds
recommendation.body: Keep a short bound only for commands proven to be quick and use a demonstrably safe bounded strategy for package-manager work.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged timeout work is the closest available history signal for choosing safe synchronous subprocess bounds.
